findings.description: Adversarial findings using symbol anchors and anchor_line are silently excluded from recall. The extractor accepts neither anchor_line nor the file portion of a symbol anchor.
findings.failure_mode: A finding such as {"anchor":"src/handler.py:handle_request","anchor_line":42} produces only a nonnumeric citation, which citations() discards. Correct defects caught exclusively by adversarial review therefore receive no recall credit.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract the file from symbol anchors and combine it with anchor_line and optional anchor_line_end, while retaining support for existing numeric anchors.

findings.description: Gate accuracy can treat a timed-out test process as passing because all_pass() ignores both rc and timed_out.
findings.failure_mode: If pytest prints a passing summary and then hangs during interpreter shutdown, such as while waiting for a leaked non-daemon thread, run_suite records rc=124 and timed_out=true while retaining passing counts. This call still marks an APPROVED verdict accurate. Refactor suite-green checks have the same problem.
findings.suggested_fix: Require rc == 0 and timed_out == false in all_pass(), and apply the same completion checks when determining self-check success.

findings.description: remove_path() walks a directory and calls os.chmod(os.path.join(r, d), 0o700) on every entry in `ds`. os.walk(followlinks=False) still lists symlinks-to-directories in `dirs` (it just does not descend), and os.chmod follows symlinks. The `final` grading tree is built by copy_tree(), which deliberately recreates every symlink from the agent's sandbox verbatim (lines 283 and 294), including absolute ones. So an agent-planted `ln -s /some/dir x` in the sandbox becomes a symlink in <run-dir>/grading/final, and the next remove_path() over that tree (fresh_dir(grading) on a re-grade, put_file()->remove_path() when a grader_protected directory is restored over the agent's version, or remove_path(SCRATCH) in self-check) chmods the symlink TARGET to 0o700. In host mode the grader user owns the sandbox, the run's transcripts/ and eval/ dirs, the repo checkout and ~/.claude, all of which are reachable targets; in container mode the chmod still runs on the host. The header states the grader writes only <run-dir>/grading/ and the --out file (DEC-0413); this mutates permissions of arbitrary grader-writable directories chosen by the graded agent.
findings.failure_mode: An agent (or an adversarial arm in this very ablation) creates a symlink to a directory the grader user owns; grading or re-grading that run silently drops group/other permissions on that directory (e.g. a shared fixture dir, the suite root, another run's directory), breaking later readers and violating the stated write boundary.
findings.suggested_fix: Never chmod through a symlink: in the walk, skip entries where os.path.islink(full) is true (or iterate with os.scandir and entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)). Alternatively only chmod when the lstat mode lacks owner write/exec, and leave symlinks alone; shutil.rmtree already unlinks symlinks without following them.

findings.description: Both executors strip the current directory from sys.path: `python3 -I -s -m pytest` (container) and `python3 -P -m pytest` (host). The one thing `python3 -m pytest` provides over `pytest` is cwd on sys.path, which tests in flat layouts (no root conftest.py, no tests/__init__.py chain) rely on for `from tools.x import y`. seed-bugfix-tasks.sh and seed-refactor-tasks.sh prove their tasks with the plain test_command (`python3 -m pytest -q <dirs>` under env -i, no -P), so a task can pass its seeding proof yet fail collection under the grader with ModuleNotFoundError. With a collection error every hidden test is expanded to `bad`, giving 0/N for every arm identically, which the ablation cannot distinguish from a universally hard task unless --self-check reference is run on the same host/image.
findings.failure_mode: Grader and seeder disagree on the import environment; tasks that are green in the proof grade as 0 passed across all arms, or host-mode grades differ from container-mode grades for the same run.
findings.suggested_fix: Either run the seeding proof with the exact shaped argv (share shape_command logic with seed_tasks.py), or keep cwd importable in the grader (drop -P/-I and rely on -s/-E plus the read-only tree), and make validate-suite/self-check reference mandatory before freeze.

findings.description: For build tasks in --self-check base the PASS condition is `h['passed'] < h['total'] and suite_green`. When the test command cannot run at all (pytest missing from the image, python3 -P unsupported, `-I -s` hiding the pytest install, yq/collection crash) run_suite() returns parse_error=True with passed=0 and total=max(static,1), so passed < total and the base self-check reports PASS. The reference self-check does require `not parse_error`, but base alone gives a false green for a task whose grading environment is broken, and the header documents base as 'PASS when at least one hidden test fails'.
findings.failure_mode: An author runs `--self-check base` on a task whose test command crashes and sees PASS; the environment defect surfaces only later, or never if only base is checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Require `not h['parse_error'] and not h['timed_out']` in the base PASS condition (same for the refactor branch's structural check), and surface parse_error in the evidence string.

findings.description: regression_command is executed on `final` and `base` only after prepare() has overlaid the hidden tests, so when the regression command sweeps a directory that also receives hidden tests (e.g. `python3 -m pytest -q tests/` with hidden dest tests/unit/test_x.py) the hidden cases are counted in regressions.base/final totals, and base.passed < base.total even on a pristine fixture. Self-check base then computes suite_green from r['final'] on the overlaid fixture, where the hidden tests fail by design, and reports FAIL for a correct task. The header describes the base tree as 'the baseline for regression_command' and self-check base as 'the fixture suite is green'.
findings.failure_mode: Any build task whose regression_command covers the hidden tests' destination directory fails `--self-check base` and reports inflated regression totals; authors are pushed to set regression_command null (as the seeders already do), losing regression tracking.
findings.suggested_fix: Run regression_command against the trees before the hidden overlay (copy, run regression, then prepare), or build a separate base/final copy for the regression run with only grader_protected restored.

findings.description: The header states verdict_accuracy_per_gate is false for a gate without a trailer and null only for a gate that did not run. In the build branch a gate whose feedback file exists (v != None) but whose snapshot cannot be extracted (missing IMPLEMENT/FIX1.bundle, index.json entry absent or non-hex, bundle prerequisites unmet) is skipped with `continue`, leaving acc[gate] = None, so a gate that ran is reported as not having run and verdict_accuracy falls back to the other gate. Separately, `verdict.value` can be the literal string "none" when the audit file exists without a trailer, while the header documents only APPROVED/CHANGES_REQUIRED or null.
findings.failure_mode: Runs with a broken or missing snapshot are indistinguishable from runs where the gate never executed, biasing verdict_accuracy aggregates in runs.jsonl toward the gates that happened to have snapshots.
findings.suggested_fix: Record a distinct outcome (e.g. verdict_accuracy_per_gate[gate] = false with a `snapshot_missing` list, or an explicit null-with-reason field), and map the trailer-less "none" to null in `verdict.value` while keeping it in `verdicts`.

findings.description: tf.extractall(tree, filter=keep) and tarfile.data_filter require Python 3.12 or the 3.8.17/3.9.17/3.10.12/3.11.4 backports, and the host executor's `python3 -P` requires 3.11+. On an older interpreter extractall raises TypeError (unexpected keyword 'filter'), which the top-level handler turns into exit 2 'internal error' for every run that has a review or audit verdict, and host-mode pytest exits 2 on `-P` yielding parse_error for every tree. The header only guarantees behaviour on the Sprint 258 image.
findings.failure_mode: On a grading host with an older python3 every run with a gate verdict is ungradeable (exit 2) and host-mode grades are uniformly 0 passed with parse_error, with no clear message pointing at the interpreter version.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert sys.version_info >= (3, 12) (or feature-check hasattr(tarfile, 'data_filter')) at startup and fail with a GradeError naming the requirement; for host mode choose -P only when the interpreter supports it.
